section_summary: This section chiefly records Japanese notifications of warship keel layings and completions under the London Naval Treaty of 1930, with State Department acknowledgments and copies forwarded to the Navy Department. It also covers approval of a Westinghouse machinery sale, reports on Japanese naval building plans and budgets, and a notification concerning the aircraft carrier Hiryu under the Washington Naval Treaty.

subfiles.title: Reported Japanese council discussion of naval armament
subfiles.about: Reports a British ambassador's account of Japanese deliberations on naval building.
subfiles.summary: Drummond relayed Sugimura's account of a council chaired by the Emperor. A senior admiral advocated freedom from naval conference restraints but reportedly promised against a costly race with the United States or Britain. Drummond also discussed Italy's naval position with Mussolini.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about a reported 55,000-ton Japanese battleship
subfiles.about: Requests comment on a press report of a large Japanese battleship.
subfiles.summary: Asks the embassy to assess a London press report.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of battleship inquiry
subfiles.about: Restates the request for comment on a reported 55,000-ton battleship.
subfiles.summary: Specifies the reported armament as twenty-one-inch guns.

subfiles.title: Embassy assessment of proposed large Japanese battleships
subfiles.about: Assesses reports that Japan might build battleships above treaty size.
subfiles.summary: Grew says the press report drew on speculative articles, while foreign naval attachés believed Japan was considering ships of 45,000 to 55,000 tons. He describes disagreement within the Japanese Navy, possible construction limits and concern about a building race. He expects firmer information only after Japan sees U.S. plans.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of embassy battleship assessment
subfiles.about: Restates the embassy's assessment of possible large Japanese battleships.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase recounts speculative press origins, attachés' belief that larger ships were being planned, competing views within the Japanese Navy, and Japan's stated response to possible U.S. construction.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Japanese naval budget discussion
subfiles.about: Points to Grew's telegram on shipbuilding and fortifications.
subfiles.summary: Cross-references telegram No. 106 from Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese ministers on naval competition and fortifications
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese Diet discussion of naval limitations and Pacific fortifications.
subfiles.summary: The Navy Minister reportedly favored another limitation conference and expressed concern about a shipbuilding race. The Navy and War Ministers also discussed the cost of competing in Pacific fortifications; the embassy knew of no concrete Japanese plan.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Diet speeches on naval expenditure
subfiles.about: Points to Grew's report on naval limitation and budget speeches.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Navy Minister expected higher expenditure without international agreements.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Japanese naval building policy
subfiles.about: Points to a report on a proposed change in Japanese naval construction policy.
subfiles.summary: Notes a reported shift toward construction suited to Japan's geography.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to British and American naval expansion report
subfiles.about: Points to a despatch on Japan's reaction to British and American expansion plans.
subfiles.summary: Notes reported Japanese preparations for increased construction.

subfiles.title: Japanese response to prospective British and American naval expansion
subfiles.about: Reviews Japanese press and official responses to reported British and American shipbuilding plans.
subfiles.summary: The despatch says Japan might enlarge construction plans if the reported battleship programs materialized, although naval authorities professed opposition to an arms race. It describes possible additions to battleships and aircraft carriers, rising budget estimates, and proposals for a wider national defense program. It also reports the foreign minister's position on agreements reached after Japan left the London Naval Conference.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to next fiscal year's naval expenditures
subfiles.about: Points to press information on Japan's forthcoming naval program.
subfiles.summary: Lists capital ships, carriers, auxiliaries, air power and equipment among expected spending areas.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to aircraft engine export license
subfiles.about: Points to a license for an aircraft engine export to the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: References license No. 2239 for a Menasco Super Buccaneer engine bound for Yokosuka.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to conversation with Captain Tayui
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram about Japan's shipbuilding program.
subfiles.summary: References a conversation with Captain Tayui at the naval attaché's home.

subfiles.title: Captain Tayui on prospective capital ships
subfiles.about: Reports Captain Tayui's comments on Japan's likely capital ship construction.
subfiles.summary: Tayui said the number of ships depended on the naval budget: perhaps one under a small two-year program, or two or more under a larger, longer program. He expected sixteen-inch guns; discussion of fourteen-inch guns was interrupted.
